note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Left-sided hearing deterioration for ~6 weeks with intermittent left-sided tinnitus and occasional mild dizziness; plan for face-to-face ear inspection within 4–5 days and patient education on tinnitus.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Patient-reported reduced hearing in the left ear.
  - Left-sided ringing in the ear (tinnitus).
  - Occasional mild dizziness/feeling off-balance (not true spinning vertigo).
- Timeline / course:
  - Symptoms present approximately 6 weeks.
  - Patient reports on-and-off pattern during this period; some triggers/modifiers noted (e.g., watching TV or listening to music affects the ringing).
  - Prior episode about 1 year ago of a hearing problem that lasted a couple of days.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Patient stated watching TV or listening to music can “solve” the ringing at times.
  - No specific exacerbating factors documented.
- Associated symptoms / review of systems:
  - No ear pain.
  - No ear discharge.
  - No fever reported.
  - No chest pain, palpitations, or severe associated systemic symptoms reported.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No ear itching documented.
  - No severe vertigo (patient described off-balance rather than spinning).
  - No fever, no otorrhea, no chest pain or palpitations.

Past Medical History:
- Prior transient hearing issue ~1 year ago, lasted a couple of days (no further details).
- No other medical conditions documented.
- Medications: none documented.
- Allergies: none documented.

Social History:
- Patient confirmed being in a private place for the consult.
- Smoking, alcohol, and substance use: not mentioned.
- Occupational or other social details: not mentioned.

Family History:
- No family history documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: none documented.
- Examination findings: no physical exam performed during this consultation; plan for in-person otoscopic exam documented.

Investigations:
- No investigations or test results reported.
- Planned: face-to-face otoscopic examination of the ears by a GP in clinic within ~4–5 days to exclude impacted wax or other visible pathology.
- Patient to receive a tinnitus information leaflet (link to be placed in the notes).

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Left-sided hearing loss with left-sided tinnitus and intermittent mild dizziness
  - Assessment: Patient-reported decreased hearing on the left for ~6 weeks with intermittent tinnitus and occasional non-spinning dizziness; cause not determined in this consult.
  - Plan:
    - Arrange face-to-face clinic appointment within approximately 4–5 days for otoscopic inspection of the left ear to exclude impacted wax or other visible pathology; admin team to schedule.
    - Provide patient with tinnitus information leaflet for education prior to clinic visit.
    - Advise patient to avoid using cotton buds to clean ears (physician counseled against this).
    - If symptoms worsen or new problems arise before the scheduled clinic visit, instruct patient to book another appointment or contact support team/clinic.
    - Not considered an emergency at present per clinician.
- Issue 2: Recurrent prior short episode of hearing loss (~1 year ago)
  - Assessment: Historical, lasted a couple of days; relevance to current episode to be evaluated at clinic examination.
  - Plan:
    - Review history and compare findings during the in-person ear exam; consider further investigations if otoscopic exam is normal (not explicitly documented in transcript).
- Issue 3: Patient education and follow-up logistics
  - Assessment: Patient expressed interest in learning about tinnitus.
  - Plan:
    - Clinician to paste link to tinnitus leaflet in the appointment notes for patient review.
    - Clinician will leave a support team phone number in notes; patient to contact admin to be slotted into clinic.
    - Clinic appointment will be with another GP who will have these notes.

General plan items:
- Send tinnitus information leaflet to patient.
- Administrative staff to schedule in-person ear exam within ~4–5 days.
- Provide support team contact in notes for scheduling or earlier concerns.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Medication list and current regular medications not documented.
  - Allergy list not documented.
  - Vital signs (HR, BP, temperature) not documented.
  - No physical exam findings (otoscopy) documented — examination planned but not yet performed.
  - No audiology testing (audiogram) or ENT referral documented; may be appropriate depending on clinic findings.
  - No specific safety-net instructions with symptom red flags documented (e.g., sudden worsening, severe vertigo, new neurological symptoms) beyond “book another appointment / contact support.”
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Patient response about cotton-bud use is ambiguous: patient said “Uh nah I'll do it.” (conflict/uncertainty noted regarding whether patient uses cotton buds).
  - Clinician misnamed patient once as “John” though patient identified as Jack Smith (nonclinical but noted).
- Transcript quality:
  - Audio/transcript overall clear and intelligible; minimal overlapping speech and no significant inaudible sections.
